notes.title: Committee maintains federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent
notes.summary: The Committee decides to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent.

source.title: FOMC statement — 2009-03-18
source.quote: The Committee will maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent and anticipates that economic conditions are likely to warrant exceptionally low levels of the federal funds rate for an extended period.

notes.title: Fed anticipates inflation running at or below 2% objective
notes.summary: The Committee anticipates medium-term inflation likely running at or below its 2 percent objective, noting subdued recent inflation despite commodity price increases.

source.title: FOMC statement — 2012-09-13
source.quote: Inflation has been subdued, although the prices of some key commodities have increased recently.

passages.quote: Inflation has been subdued, although the prices of some key commodities have increased recently.
The Committee also anticipates that inflation over the medium term likely would run at or below its 2 percent objective.

notes.title: Rate range held; low-rate guidance extended to mid-2015
notes.summary: The Committee kept the target range at 0–0.25%. It anticipated that exceptionally low rates were likely to be warranted at least through mid-2015.

source.title: FOMC statement — 2012-09-13
source.quote: In particular, the Committee also decided today to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent and currently anticipates that exceptionally low levels for the federal funds rate are likely to be warranted at least through mid-2015.

notes.title: Core PCE inflation remained near very low levels despite a slight January uptick
notes.summary: The core PCE price index rose slightly in January due to core goods, but the 12-month change stayed near very low levels seen in late 2010.

source.title: FOMC minutes — 2011-03-15

source.quote: The price index for PCE excluding food and energy (the core PCE price index) rose slightly in January, boosted by an uptick in prices of core goods after four months of declines; the 12-month change in this core price index stayed near the very low levels seen in late 2010.

notes.title: Household near-term inflation expectations rose
notes.summary: The staff review reported a substantial rise in households’ near-term inflation expectations in early March, likely because of higher gasoline prices. Longer-term expectations remained within their recent range.

source.title: FOMC minutes — 2011-03-15
source.section: Staff Review of the Economic Situation
source.quote: According to the Thomson Reuters/University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers, households' near-term inflation expectations increased substantially in early March, likely because of the run-up in gasoline prices; longer-term inflation expectations moved up somewhat in the early March survey but were still within the range that prevailed over the preceding few years.

passages.quote: According to the Thomson Reuters/University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers, households' near-term inflation expectations increased substantially in early March, likely because of the run-up in gasoline prices; longer-term inflation expectations moved up somewhat in the early March survey but were still within the range that prevailed over the preceding few years.

notes.title: US inflation running below 2 percent target
notes.summary: Staff review noted total and core PCE inflation were running below 2 percent in May, with June data suggesting similar pace.

source.title: FOMC minutes — 2017-07-26
source.section: Staff Review of the Economic Situation
source.quote: The 12-month change in overall consumer prices, as measured by the price index for personal consumption expenditures (PCE), slowed again in May; both total consumer price inflation and core inflation, which excludes consumer food and energy prices, were running below 2 percent.

passages.quote: The 12-month change in overall consumer prices, as measured by the price index for personal consumption expenditures (PCE), slowed again in May; both total consumer price inflation and core inflation, which excludes consumer food and energy prices, were running below 2 percent.
passages.section: Staff Review of the Economic Situation

passages.quote: Data from the consumer and producer price indexes for June suggested that both total and core PCE price inflation (on a 12-month change basis) remained at a pace similar to that seen in the previous month.
passages.section: Staff Review of the Economic Situation

notes.title: Staff projected PCE inflation at 2% in 2019
notes.summary: After revising its 2017 PCE inflation forecast down slightly, Fed staff still projected inflation near the longer-run objective in 2018 and at 2% in 2019.

source.title: FOMC minutes — 2017-07-26
source.quote: The staff's forecast for consumer price inflation, as measured by the change in the PCE price index, was revised down slightly for 2017 in response to weaker-than-expected incoming data for inflation.

passages.quote: The staff's forecast for consumer price inflation, as measured by the change in the PCE price index, was revised down slightly for 2017 in response to weaker-than-expected incoming data for inflation.

As a result, inflation this year was expected to be similar in magnitude to last year, with an upturn in the prices for food and non-energy imports offset by a slower increase in core PCE prices and weaker energy prices.
The staff continued to project that inflation would increase in the next couple of years and that it would be close to the Committee's longer-run objective in 2018 and at 2 percent in 2019.

notes.title: Staff judged inflation risks broadly balanced
notes.summary: Fed staff weighed downside risks, including persistent soft inflation readings, against a possible upside surprise in an economy projected to operate above potential.

source.title: FOMC minutes — 2017-07-26
source.quote: The risks to the projection for inflation also were seen as balanced.

passages.quote: The risks to the projection for inflation also were seen as balanced.

Downside risks included the possibilities that longer-term inflation expectations may have edged down, that the dollar could appreciate substantially, or that the recent run of soft inflation readings could prove to be more persistent than the staff expected.

These downside risks were seen as essentially counterbalanced by the upside risk that inflation could increase more than expected in an economy that was projected to continue operating above its longer-run potential.

notes.title: Committee maintains federal funds rate target range at 1 to 1-1/4 percent
notes.summary: FOMC members decided to keep the federal funds rate target range unchanged at 1 to 1-1/4 percent after assessing economic conditions and inflation data.

source.title: FOMC minutes — 2017-07-26
source.quote: After assessing current conditions and the outlook for economic activity, the labor market, and inflation, members decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 1 to 1-1/4 percent.

passages.quote: After assessing current conditions and the outlook for economic activity, the labor market, and inflation, members decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 1 to 1-1/4 percent.

notes.title: Committee to monitor slowing inflation closely
notes.summary: Committee members agreed to keep monitoring inflation closely in light of the recent slowing, while judging near-term economic risks roughly balanced.

source.title: FOMC minutes — 2017-07-26
source.quote: Members saw the near-term risks to the economic outlook as roughly balanced, but, in light of their concern about the recent slowing in inflation, they agreed to continue to monitor inflation developments closely.

passages.quote: Members saw the near-term risks to the economic outlook as roughly balanced, but, in light of their concern about the recent slowing in inflation, they agreed to continue to monitor inflation developments closely.

source.title: FOMC minutes — 2017-07-26

notes.title: Balance-sheet normalization planned, subject to the outlook
notes.summary: The Committee intended to begin balance-sheet normalization relatively soon, provided the economy evolved broadly as anticipated.

source.title: FOMC minutes — 2017-07-26
source.quote: They updated the postmeeting statement to indicate that while the Committee was, for the time being, maintaining its existing reinvestment policy, it intended to begin implementing the balance sheet normalization program relatively soon, provided that the economy evolved broadly as anticipated.

passages.quote: They updated the postmeeting statement to indicate that while the Committee was, for the time being, maintaining its existing reinvestment policy, it intended to begin implementing the balance sheet normalization program relatively soon, provided that the economy evolved broadly as anticipated.
